Shipped in 160ec30. Catches the target fixture at exactly api/routes/schedule/timing.py:47 in the pre-fix tree (git show eb0229b^).

Implemented as a single unified trigger rather than three separate shape matchers: any ternary or 'or' whose fallback branch evaluates to a timezone. That covers all three specified shapes and keeps ordinary defaulting silent, because the fallback being a zone is the entire signal.

One live fire surfaced in the current casey_ai tree that the issue did not anticipate: api/google_models.py:55, where an absent Google timeZone falls back to a real ZoneInfo('UTC') rather than a fixed offset. Decided to keep it firing. The value feeds datetime.combine(d, time.min, tzinfo=tz) for an all-day event, so a wrong guess moves the event to the wrong day. Alternative considered and rejected: narrowing the rule to fire only on a fixed-offset fallback or an isinstance test, which would have gone silent here while preserving every specified must-fire. Rejected because 'absent zone' is a guess too, and a real IANA fallback does not make the guess correct. The rationale now says so explicitly.

Shipped in bc63d3b. Fires three times across ../casey_ai, all of them the deliberate-bad-pattern tests anticipated in the issue: api/tests/test_local_day.py:117 and two calls on api/tests/test_multiplayer_phase6.py:458. api/date_utils.py:57 and the other direct-chaining sites are silent.

One correction during implementation. A first pass treated any .astimezone(...) as a safe conversion, which let test_local_day.py:117 through -- its receiver is assigned from .astimezone(UTC), and converting to UTC produces exactly the fixed-offset value this rule exists to catch. _is_astimezone_call now rejects an argument that is a recognisable fixed offset: a UTC or timezone.utc constant, or a timezone(...) call. A bare .astimezone() still counts as a conversion, since it targets the system zone, and an argument the rule cannot resolve is assumed to be real -- ML700 polices whether that argument was typed as a ZoneInfo in the first place.

Fixed in 0025a75. A zone counts as invented only when its identity was fixed at authoring time, so the astral/sun.py shape (tzinfo rebound to ZoneInfo(tzinfo), then date.tzinfo or tzinfo) is silent.

Three decisions were settled during the fix, the first being the one the issue deferred:

- Module-level string constants ARE resolved, so ZoneInfo(_DEFAULT_ZONE_NAME) stays flagged. The corpus evidence favoured a literal-only test (the shape occurs once in 18,589 files and is never a fallback), but that test would call two spellings of the same program different things. Correctness over the cheaper proxy, at Mike's direction.
- The exemption covers ZoneInfo alone. timezone(...) yields a fixed offset however the offset was arrived at, and a fixed offset is never the zone the caller had, so timezone(timedelta(hours=11)) is still invented. Matches the existing _IANA_CONSTRUCTORS split.
- Inline and through-a-name are treated alike. x or ZoneInfo(user.tz_name) is now silent too, rather than leaving the rule with two views of one expression. This widened the change past the issue's stated _note_zone_binding scope.

Only module-level string constants are resolved; an imported name or a local string leaves the zone looking derived. Recorded in the exemptions text rather than left as a silent limit.

Measured: 7 corpus findings before, 3 after. Four astral false positives gone, psycopg's 'return zi' and both casey_ai/db/user_ops.py findings kept. 360 tests pass (5 new).

Fixed in b2e3532. Resolution now goes through a bucket keyed on the module's final dotted component, built at ingest. Measured at 150 files with the index spanning the whole tree: per-file cost was 4.30ms at 525 modules doubling to 30.07ms at 4,200; it is now flat at 0.63ms across that range, 47x faster at the top end.

The basename key the issue originally specified would not have fixed this. Both stems of a dotted name have to be checked, so every resolution consults the __init__.py bucket, and that bucket grows with the project. Keying on the final component instead files a package's __init__.py under the package's own name, collapsing both stems into one small bucket. That is recorded in the issue as an alternative considered.
